scenarios.name: ci-headless-test-fixer
scenarios.rationale: Both use goose run with --no-session, quiet, -t, --max-turns, GOOSE_PROVIDER/MODEL and secrets-based API key, and neither invents --stdin or --profile; A uses the short -q, mentions --max-tool-repetitions and GOOSE_MAX_TURNS, and says to keep keys out of config, while B uses --quiet (equivalent) but adds extras (timeouts, </dev/null, a verify step) and omits --max-tool-repetitions and hedges on --max-turns.

scenarios.name: write-validated-recipe
scenarios.rationale: Both give a valid recipe with the right parameters, templating, builtin developer extension, `goose recipe validate`, and `goose run --recipe --params`; B explicitly states the `.yaml`-not-`.yml` requirement and adds a useful render option and notes, while A never mentions the extension rule and includes unverified flags and extra extension fields.

scenarios.name: add-mcp-extensions-config
scenarios.rationale: B uses a streamable_http extension with a uri, says Goose no longer supports SSE and that the endpoint should be migrated, and has a correct stdio filesystem entry. A configures the internal server with the deprecated `type: sse`, which contradicts the rubric, though its filesystem entry is correct.
